title: Anticipatory batch-warmup and KV-curve tuner for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: For long-context workloads the first few streaming requests to a new model variant or cold GPU exhibit high p95 tail latency and higher per-token cost because KV caches are cold and batching decisions are conservative. Existing heuristics (static prewarm policy or simple fixed prefetch) either over-fill GPU memory for some variants or under-warm for others, leading to suboptimal kernel selection and lost throughput.

Goal: Build a model-specific "KV warmup curve" generator and an anticipatory batch-warmup policy (the "KV-curve tuner") that: (1) simulates early-request KV residency patterns for Llama, Mistral, and Qwen variants with long context; (2) recommends a compact warmup token schedule (micro-prefetch + transient batch sizes) per model variant + quantization profile; (3) integrates with the runtime to trigger low-cost, short-duration warmup batches that pre-populate hot KV slots without breaking latency SLOs or oversubscribing GPU memory.

Approach summary:
- Data-driven simulator: use historical trace sampling and synthetic long-dialogue generators to approximate prefix token distributions and layer hotness. The simulator produces per-layer expected "KV occupancy growth" curves for a variant and quantization profile.
- Curve representation: store a small parametric curve (3 parameters) per model-variant/quantization combo: initial-warmup-depth, transient-batch-multiplier, decay-half-life. These parameters are estimated by fitting to simulator outputs and a small number of microbenchmarks.
- Runtime integration: add a low-impact warmup path where the scheduler can inject short, high-priority micro-batches that target the early layers most sensitive to being cold. The warmup runs with a conservative max-memory guard and can be gated behind feature flags and per-customer policies (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).
- Safety and cost controls: warmup budget quotas per minute, abort-on-memory-pressure, and fallback to on-the-fly gradual fill when resources constrained.

Why this is different: instead of static per-model prefetching, this work models the temporal shape of how KV residency grows and reasons about batching as a way to amortize prewarm latency. It emphasizes minimal memory footprint warmups and explicit curve-fitting to avoid one-size-fits-all heuristics.

Scope: prototype simulator + curve estimator + runtime hook + end-to-end benchmark on three representative variants (Llama-2-70B-long, Mistral-7B-long, Qwen-14B-long) under quantized and float32 profiles. Deliverables include a lightweight artifact (kv-warmup-mapper) and a runtime feature flag for staged rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can fit a 3-parameter occupancy curve for each tested model/quantization with R^2 >= 0.92 on microbenchmark traces
Cold-start p95 latency for a 32-token streaming request reduced by >= 18% on average across the three test variants when warmup budget <= 20ms per GPU
End-to-end per-token GPU cost (measured across 1k synthetic long-dialogue sessions) improved by >= 6% without increasing steady-state memory usage
Runtime warmup path supports per-deployment gating and aborts cleanly under memory pressure (no OOMs observed in saturation tests)
Design doc + benchmark results and a feature-flagged runtime patch merged and staged behind canary for Dedicated hosts
tasks: T1: Design simulator data format and synthetic trace generator (Maya)
T2: Implement initial simulator and curve-fit pipeline (Diego)
T3: Add runtime warmup hook and scheduler API for micro-batches (runtime infra)
T4: Create per-variant calibration harness and automation to run 100 microbenchmarks per variant/quant profile
T5: Add safety guards (memory quota, abort-on-pressure) and feature-flag plumbing
T6: Run end-to-end benchmarks and produce cost/latency comparisons versus baseline heuristics
T7: Prepare PRD, rollout plan, and run an initial Dedicated canary (SRE + Solutions Eng)
T8: Documentation: console UX for warmup tuning knobs and observability metrics (KV occupancy curve chart)
T9: Post-mortem & knobs for customer opt-out and telemetry privacy review

2026-02-25 Diego Alvarez: Fitted param curves for Qwen-14B (int8) R^2=0.94, Llama-2-70B (q4f16) R^2=0.90. Reduced microwarmup token schedule from 64->24 tokens for Qwen without losing p95 gain.

2026-03-03 Maya Chen: Memory-safety tests - added abort-on-memory-pressure and a conservative max-warmup-memory of 6% of GPU for canary. No OOMs in 24h stress run. Logging added to trace warmup abort reasons.
